title: Finite free sheaf stalks have finite coordinates
statement: For a scheme X [def-pc-scheme], finite index type I, and x in X, the stalk [def-pc-module-stalk-functor] of the free O_X-module sheaf on I [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] is linearly equivalent over O_{X,x} to the module of functions I to O_{X,x}.

source.place: Stacks Project Tag 01C6: coordinate construction for finite local trivializations; reuse of the proved localStalkEquiv helper in Sheaf.AlgebraicGeometry.FiniteLocallyFreeStalkFinrank

proof.text: Restriction to the top open preserves the free sheaf: overFunctor is a left adjoint, and mapFreeIso applies with the identity unit comparison. Apply the already proved private localStalkEquiv coordinate construction from FiniteLocallyFreeStalkFinrank to this trivialization. Its projections and finite sums are mutually inverse. This delivery exposes that construction as a public Nonempty theorem; it does not infer a linear equivalence merely from a finrank equality. Finite empty I is included.

theorem exists_finite_free_moduleStalk_linearEquiv (X : Scheme.{u})
    (I : Type u) [Finite I] (x : X) :
    Nonempty (((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor X.toRingedSpace x).obj
      (SheafOfModules.free (R := X.ringCatSheaf) I)) ≃ₗ[X.presheaf.stalk x]
        (I → X.presheaf.stalk x))
